text:
Late in a measured session, a stalled queue arose while the welfare lead was handling it. Routine queue delay at the Companion Animal Travel Desk

Passengers had arrived with calm, well-prepared carriers, and the desk was moving through normal checks for pet comfort, document review, and boarding guidance. A brief pause developed when the welcome team needed to confirm a service change before the next animal could be cleared. The delay was not caused by any distress, but it did slow the line and left a few travelers waiting longer than planned.

The welfare lead stayed with the animals and kept the tone gentle, speaking softly and giving the handlers room to settle each pet. Staff used calm, humane methods throughout and avoided crowding the carriers. The senior coordinator checked the desk ledger, recorded the service change, and passed the update to the boarding side so the next step could move forward without confusion. Clear, kind guidance was given to the waiting travelers so they knew what to expect and what to keep ready.

Once the update was confirmed, the queue resumed in order and the remaining checks were completed without further concern. Olive remained settled, and the travelers were thanked for their patience and cooperation. After the rush eased, the team reviewed the note in the ledger, confirmed that the boarding flow had returned to normal, and reminded staff to keep brief updates flowing through the welcome team early when a change appears. The follow-up was simple and practical, and the desk closed the exchange in a steady manner.
